claims.text: The starting composite contains discrete W particles or interconnected W ligaments embedded in a Cu matrix.
Untreated W–Cu interfaces undergo phase separation under high-heat-flux and irradiation conditions.
Untreated W–Cu composites form interfacial voids under operative thermal and irradiation conditions.
Phase separation and interfacial void formation degrade the thermal conductivity of untreated W–Cu composites.
A thin Ni-rich coating on W surfaces will modify the W/Cu interfacial chemistry.
The Ni-modified interface will form a stable Ni-enhanced intermetallic phase involving both W and Cu.
The Ni interlayer will enhance atomic interdiffusion between W and Cu.
Enhanced interdiffusion will produce a coherent, finely dispersed Ni-rich intermetallic or solid-solution phase.
The Ni-rich interfacial phase will reduce interfacial energy.
The modified interfacial region will reduce the number of void-nucleation sites.
A Ni interlayer will improve wettability and bonding between W and Cu.
The Ni interlayer will produce a stable, chemically graded W/Cu interface that relieves local strain.
The chemically graded interface will suppress the thermodynamic driving forces for phase separation and void formation.
The stabilized interface will preserve continuous thermal-conduction paths during cyclic thermal loading and irradiation-induced damage.
Ni-coated W–Cu composites will have a lower interfacial-void density than identically processed untreated composites.
Ni-coated W–Cu composites will exhibit less interfacial phase separation than untreated composites.
Ni-coated W–Cu composites will have higher effective thermal conductivity than untreated composites under representative heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
The intervention is expected to be effective at approximately 500–1000 °C in irradiation regimes relevant to plasma-facing-material and cooling-component joints.
Extreme irradiation or prolonged thermal cycling may destabilize the Ni-induced interfacial phase and limit the intervention's effectiveness.
Reactive interfacial coatings are known to enhance bonding in metal composites.
